entry.title: Rust changed my (superficial) way of thinking
entry.summary: This might sound like another clickbait article shilling Rust, but it isn't. I've also been in the same spot as you, wondering why there is so much hype with Rust, because at the beginning, it seemed like just another low-level language like C++. But it's not. Nowadays, many programmers use exclusively programming languages with a garbage collector (Java, Go, Python, etc.) and often overlook how memory is managed to make all of this possible. The GC is seen as some kind of "black box" that does some magic with the program's memory. But then we have low-level languages like C or C++, that don't have a GC and instead have you allocate/deallocate memory manually. entry.title: Explore PHP 8.5 Features, Enhancements & Key Updates Today
entry.summary:
Have you ever wondered what makes PHP powerful in 2025? The new PHP 8.5 Features are set to revolutionize how you write code! Think of it as upgrading from a bicycle to a motorcycle – you’re still getting where you need to go, but the journey just became a whole lot smoother and faster. Scheduled for release on November 20, 2025, PHP 8.5 isn’t just another version bump. It’s a carefully crafted collection of features that address real-world developer pain points. From cleaner function chaining to smarter error handling, this release focuses on making your daily coding life better. Remember those nested function calls that look like mathematical nightmares? PHP 8.5 introduces the pipe operator (|>) – your new best friend for writing clean, readable code. Instead of writing: $result = ucfirst(trim(str_shuffle(strtoupper('Hello World')))); You can now write: $result = 'Hello World'
Why does this matter? Think of it like reading a recipe. The pipe operator lets you follow the flow from left to right, making your code as easy to read as a cooking instruction. This isn’t just syntactic sugar – it’s a fundamental shift toward more functional programming patterns. The pipe operator comes with some important ground rules: Each function must accept only one required parameter Functions with by-reference parameters aren’t supported It works with any callable: functions, methods, closures, and classes with __invoke Read Full Article: https://serveravatar.com/php-8-5-features/
